name: Warrantor Action Receipt (WAR)
note: Golden vectors for the v4 contract freeze. Schema-level cases below are machine-verified against Draft 2020-12 and MUST all produce the stated result. Semantic cases require a verifier implementation and cannot be caught by schema validation alone — they are listed here as normative requirements for the conformance harness.

baseline.description: Minimal well-formed pre_commit receipt, mediated mode, routine tier.

schema_cases.reason: A post_commit receipt with no outcome cannot establish that evidence preceded the effect.
Critical actions require non-delegable human authority in the chain.
The atomic phase collapses the commit gate and is permitted only for reversible, routine operations.
A receipt that does not declare its enforcement mode cannot be bounded in what it claims.
Artifact identity is an algorithm-prefixed content digest; names and free strings are not identity.
Warrantor verifies established delegation token formats; it does not accept bespoke ones. Prevents silent re-invention of identity standards.

semantic_cases.setup: chain has two links: link A capabilities ['tool:read','tool:write'], link B capabilities ['tool:read']; effective_capabilities claims ['tool:read','tool:write']
semantic_cases.requirement: The verifier MUST recompute the intersection (['tool:read']) and reject on mismatch. Authority is the intersection, never the union.

semantic_cases.setup: effective_capabilities is correct but intersection_proof.result_digest does not correspond to the chain
semantic_cases.requirement: The verifier MUST recompute links_digest and result_digest from chain[] and reject on mismatch.

semantic_cases.setup: a valid receipt is re-presented after expires_at, and separately re-presented within a different task context
semantic_cases.requirement: Reject on expiry without further checks; reject on nonce + receipt_id uniqueness across contexts.

semantic_cases.setup: artifacts.tools[0].canonical_resource_id is a caller-supplied string rather than the provider-resolved identifier
semantic_cases.requirement: Policy MUST key off provider-resolved identifiers only.

semantic_cases.setup: a receipt with enforcement_mode = advisory is presented as evidence of containment
semantic_cases.requirement: The verifier MUST refuse any non-bypassability or containment claim from an advisory receipt.
MUST NOT pass silently. The logbook reads clean while the sealed recorder disagrees — the signature of a swapped model artifact. Surface as a distinct alarm state.

semantic_cases.setup: same model name and version, different digest from the one attested
DSSE signature alg does not match the key type
semantic_cases.requirement: Reject. Algorithm is explicit in every receipt and MUST be checked, never inferred.

semantic_cases.setup: the delegation chain verifies correctly, but the root key appears on the revocation list
semantic_cases.requirement: Reject and invoke the containment path. Intersection is sound only while the root is honest; this is the failure mode the spec names explicitly.

semantic_cases.setup: a receipt asserting v1.0 semantics is presented to a v2.0 verifier
semantic_cases.requirement: Reject. Version downgrade must not silently drop the authority-intersection and enforcement-mode requirements introduced in v2.0.

semantic_cases.setup: receipt carries a critical extension the verifier does not understand
semantic_cases.requirement: Fail closed. An unrecognized critical extension is a denial, not a warning.
